newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 24.

text.p: Random roadblocks nab fine defaulters: Court officials began using random roadblocks on Monday to catch people owing fines. Page 1.

SFO report on Morgan may clash with Budget: The government still does not know if the issuing of the Serious Fraud Office report into Aotearoa Television Network, where NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan was a director, will clash with Thursday's unveiling of the coalition's first Budget. Page 2.
Defence spending too low, says Moore: Labour foreign affairs spokesman Mike Moore on Monday lent his voice to Foreign Affairs Minister Don McKinnon's call for more defence spending. Page 2.
Little faith in Budget forecasts: The economy and the government's books will be much worse than the figures expected in Thursday's Budget, according to a survey of economists out on Monday. Page 11.

ACC executive sought: ACC hopes to choose a new chief executive in the next two to three months. Former chief exeuctive Gavin Robins was sacked after an internal inquiry revealing "unsatisfactory aspects of his performance". Page 11.

Markets expect easing in Reserve Bank aims: The markets are expecting the Reserve Bank to ease its desired monetary conditions by 50 or 75 basis points when it releases its monetary policy statement on Friday.
Skellerup bonds do better: A measure of confidence flowed back into Skellerup bonds on Monday as the yield fell from 30 percent to 20 percent.

Saturn signs up mystery US partner: Telephone and cable television company Saturn Communications expects a boost to its finances and technical expertise when a United States telephone company takes a significant minority shareholding.

Wind show to breeze through heartland: Wind-turbine developer Vortec Energy will conduct a nationwide road show to explain and market its $10 million share issue after attracting plenty of initial interest but few dollars.
Heinz takes Tegel off the market: Heinz Wattie had taken the for sale sign off its Tegel Chicken business Tegel Foods manager Peter Lucas confirmed on Monday.

Alarm sales soar after fire deaths: A Christchurch smoke-alarm supplier was overwhelmed on Monday with a 50-fold increase in demand for its product from retailers throughout the country after a spate of deaths in domestic fires. Page 1.

Infratil bullish on electricity: More electricity assets were likely to be privatised, Lloyd Morrison, chief of the firm that manages Infrastructure and Utilities NZ (Infratil), said on Monday. Page 29.

ASB, aged 150, about to launch on the Internet: The marking of the founding of the country's first savings bank by two Auckland merchants comes three weeks before the ASB releases its Internet services to the market. Page 29.
